detailed_rationale:
Central Bank of India is a public-sector bank with the Government of India as an overwhelming ~81% shareholder (stable since 2017), organized across Treasury, Corporate/Wholesale and Retail Banking. Per the financial-sector exemption, leverage itself is not the concern for a bank - asset quality is, and the trend there is genuinely encouraging: Net NPA has fallen from 1.75% (Sep-2023) to roughly 0.45-0.51% now, Gross NPA sits at ~2.7% (improving), and CRAR is a healthy 16.13%, comfortably above regulatory minimums. TTM profit (quarters ending Jun-2026) grew ~6.8% YoY and TTM revenue grew ~9.4% YoY (matching our CSV figure closely), a modest but real growth trend, not spectacular but consistent with the bank's 45.9% 5-year profit CAGR reflecting the broader PSU-bank turnaround since the sector's post-2018 NPA-cleanup cycle.

One item worth flagging plainly: Mar-2026 net profit (Rs.748 Cr) was notably lower than the surrounding quarters (Rs.1,234-1,325 Cr) - PSU banks commonly take additional Q4 provisioning to true up full-year targets, which could explain this, but I could not confirm the specific driver from the sources available to me, so I am noting it as an observed dip rather than asserting a cause. Separately, the AGM approved a large ~Rs.7,000 Cr equity raise (Aug-2026) - against a market cap of only ~Rs.28,485 Cr, this is a meaningful capital raise, plausibly aimed at strengthening capital buffers and/or reducing the government's stake toward minimum-public-shareholding norms; either way it is a real, near-term dilution event for existing per-share metrics.

Valuation is deep-value: PE of ~6.24x and P/B of ~0.70x (trading below book) with a ~3.8% dividend yield - among the cheapest names in this batch on conventional multiples, and the value_score in our data (80.4) reflects that. Reverse-DCF: at 0.7x book with genuinely improving asset quality and a well-capitalized balance sheet, the market is pricing in either continued execution risk typical of PSU banks (structurally lower ROE than private-sector peers) or simply has not yet re-rated the improved asset-quality story - either way, the discount looks larger than the credit-quality trend alone would justify.
recommendation_rationale: Quant reads Sell on the 1-year lens (final_score_1y ~33.7, likely driven by a low quality_score of 21.0 reflecting structurally modest PSU-bank ROE). I am rescuing this to Hold: per the financial-sector exemption, the metrics that actually matter for a bank - asset quality and capital adequacy - are both genuinely improving (NNPA nearly halved over two years, CRAR a healthy 16.13%), the stock trades at a deep discount to book (0.70x) with a solid dividend yield, and profit/revenue growth, while modest, are real and positive. The main risks (an unexplained Mar-2026 profit dip, and near-term dilution from the Rs.7,000 Cr capital raise) are real but do not, in my judgment, outweigh the improving credit story and the valuation cushion - a rescue, not a mismatch.
summary: Central Bank of India is a government-owned public-sector bank whose asset quality has improved substantially over the past two years, alongside a healthy capital-adequacy ratio and a deep-value valuation (trading below book value with an attractive dividend yield). A large capital raise is planned, which will dilute existing shareholders somewhat, and one recent quarter's profit came in notably lower than the rest without a confirmed explanation. On balance we rate this a Hold, given the genuinely improving credit trend and cheap valuation outweigh the near-term dilution and data gaps.
positive_para: Asset quality has improved markedly - Net NPA down from 1.75% to roughly 0.5% over about two years - alongside a healthy 16.13% capital-adequacy ratio, a valuation at just 0.70x book value, a ~3.8% dividend yield, and consistent government ownership (~81%) providing implicit stability. Profit and revenue are both growing at a real, if modest, high-single-digit pace, continuing the sector-wide PSU-bank turnaround from the post-2018 NPA-cleanup cycle.
negative_para: Return on equity remains structurally modest for a PSU bank (10.8% 3-year average), Mar-2026 profit came in noticeably lower than surrounding quarters without a confirmed explanation from the sources I could access, and a large ~Rs.7,000 Cr equity raise is approved and pending - a meaningful dilution event relative to the bank's ~Rs.28,485 Cr market cap that will need to be absorbed before per-share metrics normalize. Five-year sales growth of under 10% also shows this remains a slow-growing, government-directed lender rather than a share-gaining challenger bank.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At 0.70x book value with Net NPA down to roughly 0.5% and CRAR at a healthy 16.13%, the market appears to be pricing either continued PSU-bank execution risk (structurally low ROE versus private peers) or has simply not yet re-rated the improved credit story - the discount looks larger than the asset-quality trend alone would justify, making this closer to cheap than fair. Growth is well below the 25% hypergrowth threshold, so no dilution/ROE-tier note applies in the way the skill intends, though note the pending Rs.7,000 Cr capital raise is itself a real, separate dilution event to track.
